: J U D G M E N T :
1.
This claim petition is filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for grant of compensation.
2. Respondent no. 1 is the driver, Respondent No. 2 is the owner, Respondent No. 3 is the Superdar and Respondent no. 4 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Case of the Claimant:
3. Claimant has stated in this claim petition that on 08.03.08 he was traveling in a tourist bus bearing no. RJ13 PA0052 and he was coming from Hissar to Delhi.

When the bus reached near BrahiBahadurgarh Railway Crossing at around 8.00 a.m., the railway crossing gate was left open by mistake of the gateman and the tourist vehicle and other vehicles were crossing the railway line.
At that time, Awadh Assam Express no. 5610 came from Rohtak side and struck the above said tourist bus as a result of which the claimant got grievous injuries.

4. It is stated that the claimant suffered fracture mandible (multiple) (Communited), fracture maxilla, fracture orbit floor, fracture scapular, loss of lower molar teeth (left side), bruises and muscular spasms on back and abdomen, 2 clear cut lacerated wounds below chin and below mandible left side, clear cut lacerated wound on the post aspect of Rt. Forearm just below the elbow.
5. It is stated that firstly the injured was taken to General Hospital, Bahadurgarh.
Thereafter, he was referred to PGI Rohtak and thereafter to M.A. Medical College and Hospital, Agroha and finally to Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Rajender Nagar, New Delhi for the treatment.

sentences.text: 6. Claimant has stated that FIR No. 32/08 under Section 279, 337, 338, 304 A and 427 of IPC and under Section 175 of The Railways Act, 1989 was registered at P.S. Rohtak regarding accident in question.
7. It is stated that the claimant was 24 years of age at the time of accident and was a final year student of MBBS at the time of accident.

Claimant has stated that he had spent Rs. 1,50,000/ on his treatment from 08.03.08 to 12.03.08.
8.
It is stated that due to this accident the claimant lost one academic year and he was on liquid diet for two months which resulted in severe weakness.
9. Claimant claims that he has spent Rs. 50,000/ on conveyance and Rs. 20,000/ on special diet.

Claimant has stated that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Respondent No. 1.
10.

Claimant has alleged that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of Respondent No. 1 and therefore he claimed a compensation of Rs. 5 lacs with interest @ 12% p.a.

Case of Respondent No. 1, 2 and 3:
11.
Respondent No. 1, 2 and 3 were proceeded exparte and no reply was filed on their behalf.

Case of Respondent No. 4:
12.

Respondent No. 4 filed its written statement and stated that unless and until it is proved that the alleged offending vehicle bearing no. RJ13PA0052 bus was having a fitness certificate and valid permit to ply the said vehicle in Delhi/accident place, no liability can be fastened upon the answering respondent.
13. It is also stated that on the date of accident driver of the bus was not holding a valid and effective driving license.
Therefore, insurance company has no liability to pay the compensation.
14. It is also stated that in this case, the bus had struck against the train and there is a possibility that claimant has already received compensation from Railways Tribunal.

15. Rest of the contents of claim petition were denied but it was admitted that vehicle no. RJ13 PA0052 bus was insured with the answering insurance company for a period from 29.03.07 to 28.03.08 in favour of M/s. Kataria Travels Pvt. Ltd.
16.

From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed:
1) Whether, petitioner Tanuj Sehrawat have sustained injuries on his person in an accident which took place on 08.03.2008 caused due to negligent driving of the vehicle bearing registration number RJ13 PA0052 being driven in a negligent manner by respondent Jaskaran, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 4?
OPP 2) In case, issue no. 1 is decided in affirmative then to what amount of compensation, petitioner is entitled and from whom?
OPP 3) Relief.

Evidence on behalf of Claimant:
17. Claimant entered in the witness box as PW1 and deposed similar facts in his evidence by way of affidavit as were already stated by him in his claim petition.
18. Claimant deposed that due to accidental injuries, he could not attend regular classes which resulted in loss of study for three months.
19. Discharge card of Maharaja Agrasen Medical College and Hospital, Agroha, Hissar, Discharge Summary of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and other treatment record of the claimant was proved as Ex.

20.
In cross examination, claimant deposed that he has not received any claim from the Railways Tribunal.
He denied any knowledge regarding inquiry conducted by Railways Tribunal as per which it was held that the accident took place due to negligence of Railways Guard.
He denied a suggestion that the accident took place due to negligence of employees of railways.

He deposed that he had passed final year of MBBS Exam in the same year in which he had met with the accident and he has not placed on record any documentary evidence to show that he had to remain absent for three months from his regular classes due to accidental injuries.
21.
Other suggestions contrary to his case were denied by him.

22. On behalf of insurance company, its Administrative Officer Sh. S.C. Mahajan entered in the witness box as R3W1 (he should have been described as R4W1 instead of R3W1), notice sent to the driver, owner and superdar under Order 12 Rule 8 of CPC was proved as Ex. R3W1/1.
In the notice served upon other respondents, insurance company had called upon them to produce permit and driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Postal receipts as per which this notice was sent were proved as Ex. R3W1/23 and AD Card showing that the notice was received by the driver was proved as Ex. R3W1/4, letter of insurance company dated 17.11.11 from Bikaner Branch to Delhi Branch was proved as Ex. R3W1/5, report of Investigator stating that there was no authorisation to drive vehicle in Haryana was proved as Ex. R3W1/6 and report of District Transport Officer, Bikaner stating that authorisation was not renewed after 31.05.07 was proved as Ex. R3W1/7.
23.

Second witness examined on behalf of insurance company was Chief Office Superintendent,
Safety Northern Railway Head Quarter, Baroda House, New Delhi who produced inquiry report regarding accident which took place on 08.03.08.
Copy of this report was exhibited as Ex. R3W1/1.
As per Inquiry Report, gateman was at fault and his negligence was well established.
(This witness was described as R3W1 whereas he should have been described as R4W2).

24. Third witness examined on behalf of insurance company was summoned from the Office of RTA,
Bikaner, Rajasthan.
(This witness was referred as R4W1 but he should have been described as R4W3).
He deposed that as per their record, the vehicle was not having authorisation which was to be renewed every year for plying the vehicle in Delhi on the date of accident.
25. No other witness was examined by any other respondents.
26. Arguments were addressed by Sh. J.S. Dagar, learned Counsel for claimant and Ms. Mamta Mayer, learned Counsel for insurance company.

27. On the basis of pleadings of parties, evidence on record and arguments addressed, issuewise findings are as under:

sentences.text: 28. Burden of proving this issue is on the claimant.

29. For succeeding in a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, it is for the claimant to prove that the vehicle which caused the accident was being driven rashly and negligently by Respondent No. 1.
30.
This is sine qua non for getting the relief.

31. Perusal of FIR No. 32/08, P.S. Rohtak shows that the accident had taken place because driver of bus no. RJ13 PA0052 was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and was hit by Awadh Assan Express Train No. 5610 at Railway Crossing.

The FIR is registered under Section 279,
337, 338 and 427 of IPC as well as under Section 175 of Indian Railways Act, 1989 which reads as under: "175. Endangering the safety of persons:

If any railway servant, when on duty, endangers the safety of any person (a) by disobeying any rule made under this Act; or (b) by disobeying any instruction, direction or order under this Act or the rules made thereunder; or (c) by any rash or negligent act or omission, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both."
32.
Police after investigation has also filed charge sheet under Section 279, 337, 338, 304 A and 427 of IPC and under Section 175 of the Railways Act, 1989.
33. Respondent No. 1 is also shown as an accused and one Sh. Sube Singh, Railways employee is also shown as an accused in the charge sheet.
Charge is framed against Respondent No. 1 under Section 279, 337, 338 and 304 A of IPC and against gate keeper of Railways under Section 175 of the Railways Act.

Part of charge framed is as under: "Lastly, on the same date, time and place you the above named accused Sube Singh violating the order of Station Master, Bahadurgarh and kept the gate no. 26C open in danger the public life at large and thus, you hereby committed an offence punishable under Section 175 of Railways Act and within the cognizance of this court".

34. It is apparent that the accident took place due to contributory negligence of Sube Singh,
Gateman of Railways as well as negligence of Respondent No. 1.
But no respondent has taken a defence of contributory negligence.
Therefore, no order can be passed on the basis of contributory negligence of gateman of Railways.
35. Perusal of site plan shows that offending vehicle was at Railway Crossing when the accident took place.
So much so even, claimant has also stated in claim petition that gateman had left railway gate open by mistake.

sentences.text: So far as negligence of Respondent No. 1 is concerned, in view of framing of charge against him under Section 279, 337, 338 and 304 A of IPC, negligence of Respondent No. 1 is also made out.

37. Moreover, in the case of Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors.: 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case.

entities.text: Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors.: 1999 ACJ 634
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, but in a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in a civil case.
No doubt before the tribunal there must be some material on the basis of which the tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to be decided for awarding compensation.
But the tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt the nicety of a civil or of a criminal case.
After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society."

38. This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S.
General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh: 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement.

sentences.text: It was noted that there is nothing on record to show that the claimant had any enmity with the driver of offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case.
39. Therefore, this issue is decided in favour of claimant and against the respondents.
ISSUE NO. 2:

40. In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., ACJ 2011 (Vol. I), following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims:
(i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., ACJ 2011 (Vol. I)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
(ii) Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads.
They are pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.

Pecuniary damages have three sub heads which are :
(i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) (a) Loss of earning ( and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b)
loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses.

Non pecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities (and /or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

(ii)(a) and (iv).

sentences.text:
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii)
(b), (iii) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
41.
Claimant was treated at Maharaja Agrasen Hospital, Agroha, Hissar from 08.03.06 to 10.03.08 and thereafter he was treated at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital from 11.03.08 to 12.03.08.
He has suffered fracture left body of mandible and fracture left scapula.
Operation carried out at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital is as under: "IMF + ORIF done on 11.03.08: Part painted and draped.
Ehrlich arch bar fixation and IMF done.
Teeth in occlusion.
Local anaesthesia infilterated in lower gingivobuccal sulcus opposite 3rd molar.
Left mandibular 3rd molar extracted.
Incision given in mucosa.
Fracture site exposed, reduced and fixded with a 5 hole titanium plate using 4 screws.
Mucosal incision closed with vicryl 30.
Chin lacerations sutured with PDS 50 and prolene 40.

Chin dressing done".
42.
Therefore, for Pain and Suffering, claimant is granted a compensation of Rs. 45,000/.
43. Medical bills worth Rs. 76,525/ are on record.

Claimant is granted a compensation of Rs.
76,525/ as Cost of Treatment.
44. Claimant has not suffered any loss of his academic year due to this accident.
He has not suffered in his performance as there is no evidence that his grading was reduced in the year of accident in comparison with grading in the previous years.
There is no evidence that he could not attend his classes for three months.
There is no evidence that he has suffered disability or was on liquid diet for three months.
Therefore, no compensation can be given to the claimant on these counts.

However,
as claimant was shifted from Agroha, Hissar to Delhi for treatment, he is granted a compensation of Rs. 10,000/ for Conveyance and considering nature of injuries he is granted Rs. 10,000/ for Special Diet and Rs. 10,000/ for Attendant's Charges.

45. Therefore, total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs. 1,51,525/ which will be paid with interest @ 7.5% p.a. (this is the rate of interest which is being awarded by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi at present) from the date of filing of this claim petition which is 23.01.10 till its deposit.
46. Next question is which respondent is liable to pay this compensation to the claimant.

sentences.text: Insurance company has summoned a witness from RTO, Bikaner who has deposed that the authorisation of permit which is to be renewed year to year was not got renewed after 31.05.07 and as on the date of accident, the permit authorisation was not renewed, it is a case of plying the vehicle without any valid permit.
48. Insurance company had served a notice upon driver, owner and superdar to produce permit.
However, even then no such permit was produced which gives an interance that the vehicle was being plied on the road without a valid permit.

Therefore, in the first instance compensation will be paid by insurance company but it will have liberty to recover the same from the owner/insured/
Respondent No. 2 by taking appropriate steps before this Tribunal.
49. Copy of award be given dasti to all the parties.
50. File be consigned to the Record Room.
